Dylan / team — drafted recommended contract language and redline summary below. High level guidance: keep audit rights narrow and operationally prescriptive to avoid open-ended inspection requests. Key points:

1) SOC 2 reference: reference Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report in the Order Form Appendix and state that the SOC 2 report (as of the report date) satisfies the customer's audit right for the controls in scope. Add a mutual confidentiality carve-out for sections we redact.

2) Pen test clause (customer-run):  add a clause that permits a single, timeboxed, customer-commissioned penetration test per 12-month period against a staging environment that mirrors production. Requirements should include: 1) 30 days' prior notice; 2) submission of a test plan and list of tools; 3) mutually agreed scope and out-of-scope endpoints; 4) a maximum blast-radius policy (no weaponized malware, no social engineering); 5) requirement that test results are provided to Redwood under an NDA and used solely for remediation.

3) Evidence cadence & data: provide monthly aggregated operational logs (date ranges + tokenized identifiers) and a quarterly ‘assurance snapshot’ (summary of incidents, mitigations, patch dates). Include an explicit statement that raw customer data is not exported as part of standard evidence delivery; any additional data extracts require a separate Narrow Data Access Addendum and approval.

4) Request tracking: include a 10-business-day turnaround SLT for routine evidence requests and a separate escalation path for time-sensitive compliance audits.

I've attached the redline PDF with inline edits. If legal wants to be more flexible on one-off additional evidence we can gate it through a signed addendum with defined scope and cost.

-Laura

Adding the security operations perspective and a draft pen-test ops plan. TL;DR: staging access is fine but we need to lock down credentials, rotate keys post-test, and ensure data masking; also we prefer a test agent model vs full network-level scans for reduced blast radius.

Operational details to include in the playbook:
- Environment: isolated staging in us-east-1, tenant-mirror of production (no live PHI).
- Windowing: 72-hour window, customer to nominate start date; Redwood will assign a point-of-contact and an on-call engineer for the window.
- Access: time-limited service accounts (least privilege) + ephemeral SSH jump host (logged).
- Evidence artifacts we can provide post-test (standard): host-level logs (7-day snapshot), application-level telemetry (aggregated), vulnerability scan summary, and remediation plan.
- Out-of-scope: attacks that attempt to exfiltrate customer data, social engineering of Redwood staff, and active exploitation of third-party payment processors.

I'll attach the pen-test plan doc with the standard ops checklist. If Brightway wants to run an authenticated web app test, request that they share the toolset in advance so we can verify allowed modules.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Security Engineering
